items.prompt: White to move. Black's bishop pins the knight on f3 against the queen. Find a sound move.
hints: The knight on f3 cannot leave without a cost. What stands behind it on the diagonal?
Several moves are sound. Which ones keep the knight where it is and add a second job to a pawn or a piece?
Look at c3, Nbd2, Be2 or Bb5.
items.explain: The knight on f3 is pinned: if it leaves, the bishop takes the queen. Several moves are within 0.3 pawn of the best (c3 backs up d4, Nbd2 adds a defender, Be2 and Bb5 develop the bishop). Moving the pinned knight is the one family that is clearly worse.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawn on c4 attacks d5. Find a sound reply.
hints: Count the attackers and defenders of d5.
The pawn on c4 attacks d5 once; Black has two defenders already. Which move develops a piece and keeps the structure?
Look at Bd6, Bb4+, Bxb1, dxc4, Nbd7, Nc6 or Nh5.
items.explain: d5 is attacked once and defended twice, so nothing is lost at once. Seven moves are within 0.25 pawn of the best at depth 16; a plan tells you which moves to compare, not the one to play. Bd6 challenges White's bishop on f4, Bb4+ develops with a check, Bxb1 trades the bishop for a knight, Nbd7 adds a defender, and dxc4, Nc6 and Nh5 are also fine.
